subject: Requesting SLO exception after unexpected autoscaling failure
messages:
From: Tina Park <tina.park@finmetrics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s and latency spike this morning

Hi Monica —

We started seeing intermittent 503s and a sustained latency increase on our integration this morning at ~08:40 PDT. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side, and the errors persisted for roughly 22 minutes before traffic returned to normal. Example requests and timestamps attached.

We rely on the "99.9% availability" SLO for peak processing; the observed window is large enough that our SLA reporting flags it as a potential credit event. Please confirm whether this aligns with any known issues on your side and whether Redwood will treat this as an eligible downtime for SLO credit.

Attachments: request-examples-07-28.csv (see lines for 08:40:12, 08:45:28, 09:01:05)

Thanks,
Tina Park
Head of Integrations — FinMetrics
T: +1 415-555-0199

Thanks for the report and the request examples. I'm sorry for the disruption. I'm opening this with our infra team immediately and will confirm the exact window and cause.

- I'll escalate to infra and ask for an authoritative downtime window and root-cause hypothesis.
- We'll check fallback routing and scaling logs.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Intermittent 503s and latency spike this morning — need verified downtime window and credit eligibility

Team —

FinMetrics reported a ~22 minute outage window starting ~2026-07-28 08:40 PDT with elevated 503s and latency. Customer uses our hosted API (prod, model: redwood-large-v2, pinned). They flagged this as a potential SLO credit event.

Ask: can infra confirm whether there was an autoscaling failure / control-plane delay that prevented additional nodes from joining? If so, provide:
- authoritative downtime window (start/end, timezone)
- percentage of requests affected vs. customer traffic during window (approx)
- cause hypothesis and whether this is a platform defect that qualifies under SLA (not customer misconfig)
- whether any exceptions (maintenance, customer misconfig) apply

Please attach raw autoscaler logs and any latency histograms. FinMetrics is requesting a formal eligibility determination and, if eligible, the credit calculation. I'll own customer comms.

Thanks — Monica
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Intermittent 503s and latency spike this morning — need verified downtime window and credit eligibility

Monica / team —

We investigated the control-plane and autoscaler logs. Summary below (high level):
- Root cause: regression in our autoscaler reconciliation loop after a recently deployed change to batching heuristics. The change caused the autoscaler to overshoot the target and then hit a retry/backoff path; new nodes did not attach for ~20 minutes in one affected cluster.
- Confirmed affected window for FinMetrics' cluster: 2026-07-28T08:40:21-07:00 to 2026-07-28T09:02:37-07:00 (22m16s).
- Impact: ~4.3% of their requests returned 503s; 16% of requests saw p95 latency rise above SLO threshold during the window.
- Exception eligibility: this is a platform-side defect unrelated to customer config => qualifies for SLO credit under our published policy.

Attachments included: error-logs-2026-07-28.txt (autoscaler traces + attach failures), slo-window-analysis.csv (request counts and latency buckets), internal-incident-84712-notes.txt (timeline).

Action items I recommend:
1) Confirm calculation for credit (we generally prorate by downtime fraction against monthly uptime SLO).
2) Offer FinMetrics a one-time service credit and a postmortem with remediation items + mitigation timeline.
3) Rollback / patch the autoscaler change ASAP (on it).

I'll follow with a short postmortem draft and a link to the internal incident board.

— Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tina Park <tina.park@finmetrics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: SLO credit eligibility and postmortem next steps (FinMetrics)

Hi Tina —

Thank you again for flagging the issue and for the request examples you provided. Our SRE team completed the initial investigation and confirmed the incident details:

- Affected window: 2026-07-28 08:40:21 PDT -> 2026-07-28 09:02:37 PDT (22m16s)
- Cause: regression in autoscaler reconciliation after a recent heuristic change; prevented timely node attachment in one cluster
- Impact to your traffic: ~4.3% 503s and an elevated p95 for ~16% of requests during the window
- Eligibility: this is a platform-side defect and therefore qualifies for SLO credit under our policy.

What we'll provide next week:
- Formal credit calculation and one-time service credit applied to your account (we prorate based on the downtime fraction).
- Postmortem document with remediation steps and timeline (draft available: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-postmortem-draft).
- Confirmation of the fix: the autoscaler patch has been deployed to the affected pool; we are monitoring and will share stability metrics.

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute review this week to walk the postmortem and credit math with your team. Proposed times: Mon 08/02 10:00 PDT or Tue 08/03 14:00 PDT — let me know what works.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We appreciate the patience and your partnership.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: support-ticket-84712.pdf, error-logs-2026-07-28.txt, slo-window-analysis.csv]
